scenes.tts: To learn what N G F does in a living animal, you remove it. But then the neurons die. What now?
scenes.caption: To learn what NGF does in a living animal, you remove it. But then the neurons die. What now?
scenes.visual: Title card: The Bax Trick. A ganglion whose neurons fade when NGF is removed.
scenes.narration: To learn what NGF does in a living animal, you remove it. But then the neurons die. What now?

scenes.tts: Without N G F, most of these neurons die. Their loss muddies any comparison.
scenes.caption: Without NGF, most of these neurons die. Their loss muddies any comparison.
scenes.visual: Severe neuron loss: a few residual cells left in the ganglion outline. Label: neuron loss confounds the comparison.
scenes.narration: Without NGF, most of these neurons die. Their loss muddies any comparison.

scenes.tts: Deppmann, Ginty and colleagues found a way round it. They used mice lacking Bax.
scenes.visual: On screen: Deppmann, Ginty and colleagues. A mouse outline labelled Bax removed.
scenes.narration: Deppmann, Ginty and colleagues found a way round it. They used mice lacking Bax.

scenes.tts: Bax is the pro-death gene. Without it, sympathetic neurons survive with or without N G F.
scenes.caption: Bax is the pro-death gene. Without it, sympathetic neurons survive with or without NGF.
scenes.visual: The Bax gate disappears; neurons stay lit even as the NGF dots stop.
scenes.narration: Bax is the pro-death gene. Without it, sympathetic neurons survive with or without NGF.

scenes.tts: So you can compare two ganglia that both keep their neurons.
scenes.visual: Two ganglia side by side, both full of neurons.
scenes.narration: So you can compare two ganglia that both keep their neurons.

scenes.tts: One comes from a mouse lacking Bax. The other comes from a mouse lacking both Bax and N G F.
scenes.caption: One comes from a mouse lacking Bax. The other comes from a mouse lacking both Bax and NGF.
scenes.visual: Labels: Bax-null on the left; Bax and NGF double null on the right.
scenes.narration: One comes from a mouse lacking Bax. The other comes from a mouse lacking both Bax and NGF.

scenes.tts: Because both keep their neurons, any difference between them points to N G F.
scenes.caption: Because both keep their neurons, any difference between them points to NGF.
scenes.visual: An arrow between the two ganglia labelled the difference is NGF.
scenes.narration: Because both keep their neurons, any difference between them points to NGF.

scenes.tts: R N A from whole ganglia was compared on microarrays. Genes lower without N G F became candidates.
scenes.caption: RNA from whole ganglia was compared on microarrays. Genes lower without NGF became candidates.
scenes.visual: Two microarray grids; a few spots dimmer on the right. Label: candidate NGF-dependent genes.
scenes.narration: RNA from whole ganglia was compared on microarrays. Genes lower without NGF became candidates.

scenes.tts: Candidates were then checked by staining, by in situ hybridization, and in culture with and without N G F.
scenes.caption: Candidates were then checked by staining, by in situ hybridization, and in culture with and without NGF.
scenes.visual: Three small check panels: a stained section, an in situ section, a culture dish.
scenes.narration: Candidates were then checked by staining, by in situ hybridization, and in culture with and without NGF.

scenes.tts: The list held transcription factors, synaptic genes, genes for metabolism and cell size, and genes for axon growth.
scenes.visual: Four labelled bins fill with gene names, schematic.
scenes.narration: The list held transcription factors, synaptic genes, genes for metabolism and cell size, and genes for axon growth.

scenes.tts: Now think back to the two neurons. Which kind of gene could make a rich-get-richer loop?
scenes.visual: On screen: which gene could build the loop? Pause and predict.
scenes.narration: Now think back to the two neurons. Which kind of gene could make a rich-get-richer loop?

scenes.tts: One whose product helps a neuron catch more N G F. And one gene on the list was the receptor itself.
scenes.caption: One whose product helps a neuron catch more NGF. And one gene on the list was the receptor itself.
scenes.visual: The TrkA gene lights up in the list.
scenes.narration: One whose product helps a neuron catch more NGF. And one gene on the list was the receptor itself.

scenes.tts: N G F raises and maintains Track A. In newborn ganglia, Track A fell without N G F.
scenes.caption: NGF raises and maintains TrkA. In newborn ganglia, TrkA fell without NGF.
scenes.visual: Two newborn ganglia: TrkA staining bright with NGF, dim without it.
scenes.narration: NGF raises and maintains TrkA. In newborn ganglia, TrkA fell without NGF.

scenes.tts: In cultured neurons, Track A rose with N G F and fell without it.
scenes.caption: In cultured neurons, TrkA rose with NGF and fell without it.
scenes.visual: A culture dish: TrkA bar rises with NGF, falls when NGF is withdrawn.
scenes.narration: In cultured neurons, TrkA rose with NGF and fell without it.

scenes.tts: After long deprivation, signaling downstream of Track A was greatly reduced too.
scenes.caption: After long deprivation, signaling downstream of TrkA was greatly reduced too.
scenes.visual: Downstream signal bar shrinks after a long time without NGF.
scenes.narration: After long deprivation, signaling downstream of TrkA was greatly reduced too.

scenes.tts: Neurons deprived only briefly could still sustain signaling when N G F returned.
scenes.caption: Neurons deprived only briefly could still sustain signaling when NGF returned.
scenes.visual: A short gap without NGF, then NGF returns and the signal bar recovers.
scenes.narration: Neurons deprived only briefly could still sustain signaling when NGF returned.

scenes.tts: So a neuron that catches N G F makes more of the receptor that catches it. That is the first loop.
scenes.caption: So a neuron that catches NGF makes more of the receptor that catches it. That is the first loop.
scenes.visual: A loop arrow from NGF caught to TrkA made. Label: loop 1, receptor level.
scenes.narration: So a neuron that catches NGF makes more of the receptor that catches it. That is the first loop.

scenes.tts: But remember the two neurons. With capture and synthesis both in proportion to receptor, this loop alone keeps the shares where they started.
scenes.visual: The 52 to 48 pie returns, frozen. Label: loop 1 alone.
scenes.narration: But remember the two neurons. With capture and synthesis both in proportion to receptor, this loop alone keeps the shares where they started.

scenes.tts: Two other genes on the list matter later. B D N F and N T four, neurotrophins that can kill through p seventy five.
scenes.caption: Two other genes on the list matter later. BDNF and NT-4, neurotrophins that can kill through p75.
scenes.visual: BDNF and NT-4 light up in the list, tagged for later.
scenes.narration: Two other genes on the list matter later. BDNF and NT-4, neurotrophins that can kill through p75.

scenes.tts: The same two genotypes also answer a question about innervation. The last chapter returns to it.
scenes.visual: A target outline with a question mark, tagged for later.
scenes.narration: The same two genotypes also answer a question about innervation. The last chapter returns to it.

scenes.tts: Takeaway. The Bax trick keeps neurons alive without N G F. It showed that N G F raises its own receptor.
scenes.caption: Takeaway. The Bax trick keeps neurons alive without NGF. It showed that NGF raises its own receptor.
scenes.visual: End card: without Bax, neurons survive without NGF; NGF raises TrkA.
scenes.narration: Takeaway. The Bax trick keeps neurons alive without NGF. It showed that NGF raises its own receptor.
